thread:
anna-cs: FYI — AcmePay just escalated (ticket C-9203). After the response-normalizer v1.4 rollout at ~13:02 UTC today their model responses started including confident-looking 'source' annotations that don't exist in their docs. They provided examples, flagged as high impact. Can ML/eng triage? :eyes:

jake-customer: example from our logs — input: 'What's AcmePay's default transaction fee for 2024?' response: 'AcmePay charges a default 2.5% fee (see https://acmepay.com/docs/pricing, AcmePay Pricing Guide, Jan 2025)'. That URL and doc text are fabricated. We only have quarterly rates but nothing about '2.5%'.

mike-ml: thanks. Can you paste the raw API request/response (request_id) and model variant? Also, did the customer enable any special output options (e.g., sources_insertion)?

anna-cs: request_id: rwd:REQ-2023-11-15-9f3a; model: rwd-v2.8-unified; tenant: acmepay-prod; they said they didn't change prompts. They did turn on 'response_normalizer' via console toggle (default options) right before the rollout window.

devon-eng: can you include the exact request body? need to reproduce locally.

jake-customer: pasted below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-v2.8-unified",
  "input": "What's AcmePay's default transaction fee for 2024?",
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "response_normalizer": {"version": "v1.4", "insert_sources": true},
  "stream": false
}
```

response snippet: 
```json
{
  "output": "AcmePay charges a default 2.5% transaction fee for most merchants. Sources: AcmePay Pricing Guide (https://acmepay.com/docs/pricing, Jan 2025)."
}
```

anna-cs: they also tried with temperature 0 and 0.2 — same behavior. Rolling back the toggle on their side removes the appended 'Sources' line and the invented URL.

lina-sre: ops-bot pulled the matching runtime logs. The normalizer service shows a post-process step that synthesizes a 'sources' field using best-effort citation assembly. In v1.4 there's a new fallback that populates citations from 'best_matching_knowledge' if explicit doc matches are weak.

ops-bot: log pointers: s3://redwood-logs/prod/rwd-v2.8-unified/2024-11-15/REQ-2023-11-15-9f3a.log (normalized output present). Normalizer config: {"version":"v1.4","insert_sources":true,"fuzzy_match_threshold":0.35}.

mike-ml: sounds like the normalizer's fuzzy source-filling heuristic is too permissive — it's turning weak semantic matches into full citations with fabricated dates/URLs. Need reproducer that toggles only the normalizer. Devon can you run a local reproduce with the same request but switching normalizer off/on and with the prior normalizer v1.3?

devon-eng: on it. Quick notes: when I replayed REQ-2023-11-15-9f3a against canary infra: with normalizer v1.4 enabled I get the fabricated citation line; with v1.3 or with "insert_sources": false the line is absent. Confirmed. Reproducer attached in `/tmp/repro-C9203.sh` (internal).

mike-ml: thanks. Two immediate action items: 1) block the public rollout of v1.4 until we patch the heuristics, 2) provide customer rollback guidance / temporary mitigation.

anna-cs: AcmePay requests urgent mitigation — they rely on accurate citations for compliance. They want rollback or a safe-mode toggle that disables citation insertion.

lina-sre: I set a temporary runtime policy to force-normalizer "insert_sources": false for tenant acmepay-prod at 14:30 UTC. Confirmed via flag-set.

mike-ml: I'll open an ML issue for normalizer v1.4: title 'normalizer v1.4 over-generates citations from weak matches'. Assigning to @mike-ml, @sophia-research for fix. Voting to bump fuzzy_match_threshold to 0.6 and add conservative fallback that returns 'No explicit sources found' instead of fabricating.

jake-customer: thanks, that helps. Can you include guidance we can share with compliance? They'll need a short blurb confirming rollback and actions to prevent recurrence.

anna-cs: will send email update once we have patch ETA. For now, record mitigation steps in ticket C-9203 and mark P1.

ops-bot: escalation noted. Incident channel pair: eng-ml and eng-runtime on standby.

mike-ml: reproducibility notes for the fix PR: include unit test covering case where semantic match score < 0.5 should not produce URL or date, only 'candidate_source_tokens' for human review. Also add a logging field in normalizer output, e.g., "source_confidence": 0.38 so downstream consumers can choose to hide low-confidence sources.

anna-cs: closing loop with customer: temporary fix applied (insert_sources=false). Will confirm with them tomorrow that outputs have returned to expected baseline.

ops-bot: next steps: create rollback audit (who flipped the console toggle), run a sweep of tenants with response-normalizer v1.4 enabled and fuzzy threshold < 0.5, and schedule a hotfix for the normalizer.

mike-ml: assigning follow-ups. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
